text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kaduna oil refinery in northern Nigeria shut down for repairs.
- Aircraft belonging to ADC airline overshoots runway at Calabar in eastern Nigeria. One person is feared dead.
- Nigeria Airways is to examine the $90 million debts it owes to creditors in Europe and America. The airline believes that some of the debts are questionable.
- Some communities in volatile southeastern Ogoniland invite Royal Dutch/Shell's oil producing unit to return. The company was driven out by sabotage in 1993.
- Maiduguri International Hotel in northern Nigeria inaugurated after 17 years of construction. The project, completed by the Borno State government cost 600 million naira.
- A four-nation meeting has opened in the Togo capital Lome, between Nigeria, Ghana, Togo and Benin over construction of a $260 million gas pipeline along the West African coast.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation seeks an extension of its approval to import fuel. Originally the approval was scheduled to end in September.
- The government has appointed Total Nigeria TOTL.LG as a consultant in the search for a solution to the problem of assuring a regular supply of refined petroleum products and then distributing them.
